title: MIHVER M0 MemoryContext
description: One immutable MemoryContext snapshot produced by exactly one authorized MemoryContext Producer invocation, per docs/contracts/MEMORY_CONTEXT.md (part of the Accepted ADR-0004). A structurally valid document is not, by itself, evidence that any pipeline stage is currently authorized to consume it, or that dependencies B/C/D are enabled — see docs/contracts/MEMORY_CONTEXT_SCHEMA_MAPPING.md. Cross-artifact reference resolution, live Brain state, and semantic content judgments are checked outside JSON Schema, where checked at all.

memory_context_id.description: This artifact's own stable identity. Together with an admitted entry's entry_id, forms the (memory_context_id, entry_id) reference pair a future, separately-authorized amendment may use to cite exactly one MemoryContext entry from another artifact. No such citation is defined or performed here.

run_id.description: The current run/invocation this MemoryContext is bound to. Distinct from run_context, which answers a different question (which project, if any) than this field (which run).

consuming_stage.description: The single stage this MemoryContext was produced for. An open identifier, not a closed enum of currently-authorized stages: whether M0_SCOPE.md actually authorizes this stage to consume MemoryContext is decided entirely by M0_SCOPE.md, never by this schema (Principle 12, Evolvability).

retrieval_query.description: The retrieval basis for this invocation. May be a literal lexical query or a structured description of a non-lexical retrieval purpose (e.g. corroborating an already-established RunContext identity); this schema does not fix a query grammar.

retrieval_time.description: When this Producer invocation retrieved and froze this snapshot. Distinct from any admitted entry's own Brain-recorded brain_created_at/brain_updated_at timestamps.

excluded_entries.description: Retrieved candidates not admitted, with their exclusion reason, preserved for audit/reproducibility. Never a source of content a consuming stage may cite or use; only admitted_entries may be used.

runContext.description: Distinguishes RunContext existing (with a project identity) from RunContext being explicitly absent. Never inferred from Brain content; never a substitute for UserIdea.

sourceRecord.description: Brain-recorded facts about the underlying memory, mechanically captured at production time. brain_type is a weak classification prior only, per MEMORY_CONTEXT.md's 'Semantic Authority Classes' section, and carries no epistemic authority by itself.

brain_type.description: inbox is never a valid brain_type for an admitted entry; inbox records are excluded from production entirely, unconditionally, on type alone.

scope.description: Either the literal value "global" or a project slug. Checked against run_context by the deterministic validator, never assumed compatible from a matching-looking value.

brain_status.description: Brain's own record lifecycle. The deterministic validator rejects brain_status "superseded" for an admitted entry (M-04); this schema alone does not, since the full Brain status vocabulary is a faithful mirror of Brain's real schema.

brain_confidence.description: The memory author's own durability/usefulness judgment at write time. Never MIHVER's own Inference-derivation or Evidence confidence; this artifact carries no such field at all, structurally preventing that conflation (M-02).

historicalCitation.description: The originating historical user-authored source a Category A entry is inspectably traced to. Structural completeness (this shape) is schema-enforced; that the citation actually, genuinely resolves to real content in the named UserIdea artifact is not re-verifiable by this single-artifact validator and remains production's own asserted judgment (mirrors UI-05's identical limitation).

classification.description: The Accepted contract's per-entry classification, assigned at production, never left to the consuming stage. Ambiguity must resolve toward less authority, never more (M-19) -- enforced where mechanically decidable by the deterministic validator, not by JSON Schema alone.

semantic_authority_class.description: Production's own descriptive semantic authority classification (Axis 3 of MEMORY_CONTEXT.md's 'Seven Independent Authority Axes'), e.g. "historical_user_statement", "prior_project_decision", "durable_project_description", "prior_architecture_outcome", "candidate_technology_knowledge", "process_guidance". Deliberately an open, non-empty string, not a closed enum: MEMORY_CONTEXT.md's 'Semantic Authority Classes' table describes these classes narratively as production's own judgment call, not as a fixed closed taxonomy, and this field must not pretend otherwise. Independent from brain_type (a weak prior only, per M-18), historical_user_category (the separate Historical User Provenance Gate axis), and influence_tier (Axis 7) -- collapsing any of these into another reproduces the force/origin/confidence collapse ADR-0002 already forbids, one layer up.

is_historical_user_statement.description: Whether production's own content inspection classifies this entry as describing a historical user statement -- decided by content inspection, never by brain_type alone (M-18).

historical_user_category.description: Required (A or B) exactly when is_historical_user_statement is true; null otherwise. A = direct, inspectably and resolvably traceable to an original historical user-authored source. B = derived/unverified: reads like a user statement but lacks that traceable linkage -- the default absent an inspectable, resolvable citation.

classification_basis.description: What in the record (which field, or which specific content) the classification rests on.

classification_method.description: Per Principle 6: a mechanical field-equality check is deterministic; reading and interpreting free-text content is heuristic (model-assisted) and must declare itself as such.

classification_ambiguity.description: Null when the classification was clean. A non-empty description of the competing readings when it was not -- an ambiguous classification never silently disappears.

influence_tier.description: The ceiling of influence this entry is authorized for, at this consuming stage. A structurally valid value here is not itself stage authorization -- see the artifact-level description and MEMORY_CONTEXT_SCHEMA_MAPPING.md.

freshness.description: A mechanical, age/lifecycle-based fact only (M-05). This artifact has no field asserting the underlying real-world claim is still true -- that question belongs to whichever mechanism actually re-verifies current facts, never to MemoryContext production.

freshness_basis.description: The mechanical basis for the flag, e.g. elapsed time since brain_updated_at versus a stated threshold.

entry_id.description: Stable identity for this entry within this MemoryContext, unique among every admitted_entries and excluded_entries entry_id in this artifact.

content.description: The memory's own content, retained as an actual copy at production time -- never merely a hash or pointer into Brain's mutable vault. This schema provides no hash-only or pointer-only alternative shape.

admission_reason.description: Explicit retrieval rationale for why this entry was admitted (M-14's 'why it was admitted or excluded... for both outcomes'), symmetric with excludedEntry's exclusion_reason. Recorded as its own durable fact rather than left to be reconstructed later from scope/status/classification/tier, which would defeat M-14's audit purpose -- those fields remain independently required for their own reasons (mechanical checks, cited authority, etc.), not as a substitute for this one.

excludedSourceRecord.description: Same as sourceRecord, except brain_type additionally allows "inbox" -- an excluded candidate may be any of Brain's eight real types, since exclusion (unlike admission) is never restricted to the seven non-inbox types.

exclusionClassification.description: Same fields as classification, minus influence_tier -- an excluded entry is never assigned an influence tier, since it was never admitted for any use. Present only when production actually attempted a classification before excluding (e.g. a fail-closed exclusion where even DISCOVERY_ATTENTION could not be defensibly assigned); null when exclusion happened before any classification was attempted at all (e.g. inbox-type exclusion, or a mechanical scope mismatch -- see M-06/M-16).

semantic_authority_class.description: Same discipline as classification.semantic_authority_class -- present whenever exclusionClassification itself is non-null (i.e. a classification was actually attempted before exclusion).

content.description: Retained actual copy, same discipline as an admitted entry's content -- Brain returns the full record for anything retrieved, whether ultimately admitted or excluded.

classification.description: Null when exclusion happened before any classification was attempted (e.g. inbox-type exclusion, or a mechanical scope mismatch), since content inspection genuinely never occurred -- distinct from freshness below, which is always mechanically computable regardless of whether classification was attempted.

freshness.description: Required, never null, even for an excluded entry: freshness is a purely mechanical, age-based fact derived from Brain's own created/updated timestamps and this invocation's retrieval time (M-05) -- it requires no content inspection at all, unlike classification, so there is no legitimate case where a retrieved-but-excluded candidate lacks a computable freshness judgment (M-14).
